items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Him and Woody were the funniest guys I ever worked for.

ctx.x: I heard you made a lot of money there.

Oh, a hundred a week. What was it — no, no, no, it paid ninety a week, ninety a week, sorry, ninety. Maybe sixty, maybe it was sixty a week, and then it went up to ninety five when we worked at the Statler chain. But I was always broke, you’re always broke. And then I went with Ted Weems right after that. And we had a good time with him. He was a great guy, great guy. Gee he was just the nicest guy you ever met. Funny. Real funny and real loose. Him and Woody were the funniest guys I ever worked for.

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: Jake was there, constantly, and Nat Pierce and Chase was there every night

ctx.x: Jake was there, constantly, and Nat Pierce and Chase was there every night, through the whole -- and if we got different trumpet players at different times, they were usually guys from Boston or New York area, who'd been in the band, or -- that was his department.
